rationale: design-import-refactor: generic change landed in Pulp per owner decision 2026-10-04; Vellum inherits (see inheritance ledger); on Graphite, SkiaSurface's persistent-scene blit and SkiaCanvas::end_layer()'s retained-layer seal now take SkSurfaces::AsImage, a view of the surface's own texture, instead of makeImageSnapshot, which on Graphite always copies; both fall back to the copy when the surface is not textureable, and Ganesh and raster keep their copy-on-write snapshot. The scene view lives only inside the blit, which is recorded into the frame's own recording before any later scene draw; the layer surface is released immediately after the seal, so the sealed image is its texture's only owner. read_current_rgba()'s synchronous fallback, taken when the asynchronous readback fails or times out, now reads an AsImageCopy of its source instead of a makeImageSnapshot, so the scene never mixes the two image APIs and Graphite no longer warns on the next blit; a process-wide set_async_readback_for_testing() seam reaches that fallback. Presented and sealed pixels are unchanged; a steady persistent-scene frame no longer encodes a full-scene texture copy and a retained seal no longer allocates a second texture. No frame, present, design-import, Chromium, packaging or authority boundary moves; the Pulp canvas and render targets have not adopted a Vellum package.
tests: ctest --test-dir build -R 'Graphite AsImage view of a surface sees later draws into it'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'SkiaCanvas Graphite layer seal shares the layer texture'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'SkiaSurface persistent-scene blit presents each frame.s own scene'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'SkiaSurface persistent-scene frames do not copy the scene'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'SkiaSurface readback fallback keeps the scene blit free of snapshot warnings'
